Subject: Level & scope heatmap: Senior LLM Inference - alignment and interviewer focus

Team —

We have a strong candidate (Asha Roy) who is moving to panel interviews for the Senior LLM Inference role. Before we lock panel slots I want a quick alignment on: scope, leveling expectations, and the debrief rubric so panel feedback is consistent.

Quick context: Asha currently leads inference performance at a mid‑sized AI infra startup (5+ people on the infra team). Resume attached. We scoped this as a Senior IC role (not staff) but there are some strong infra/distributed signals that could push to staff.

Attached: role_scope_heatmap.xlsx (one page: must-have / nice-to-have / stretch).

Asks:
- Evelyn / Markus: confirm "must-have" vs "stretch" for the role (I've suggested: production inference pipelines, latency SLO ownership, kernel/runtime tradeoffs = must).
- Markus: any red flags we should call out pre-panel?
- Panel (Jonas, Marissa, Naomi): which interview slots next week work for you? I added three proposed 90‑minute blocks (60 min interview + 30 min debrief).

Proposed interviewer focus areas (draft):
- Runtime & kernels: memory / kv cache strategies, quantization tradeoffs (Markus focus)
- System design: end-to-end inference flow, failure modes, routing/caching decisions (Evelyn focus)
- Observability & cost controls: tracing, token‑level cost attribution, batching policies (Jonas / Naomi)
- Behavioral: leadership, hiring/mentorship examples, cross-team tradeoffs (Marissa)

Attachments: Asha_Roy_Resume.pdf (PDF, 142KB), role_scope_heatmap.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)

Thanks — Priya

> Team —

Thanks Priya — agree with the high level. A few concrete adjustments from a hiring manager perspective:

1) Must-have (we should treat these as knockout items):
- Demonstrated ownership of production LLM inference pipelines (rollouts, rollback, post‑release regressions)
- Clear understanding of latency SLO tradeoffs and practical mitigations at 100s of qps
- Experience defining and instrumenting token-level cost attribution / quotaing

2) Nice-to-have (will separate senior vs staff):
- Deep kernel-level optimization (useful but not required for Senior; expected for Staff)
- Experience running dedicated GPU fleet economics negotiations (Reserved capacity products)

3) Debrief guidance: use a 1‑5 anchor and map to hiring bar: 4 = solid Senior; 5 = Staff candidate. For each focus area include a 1‑sentence tip for reviewers (I added notes in the heatmap doc).

Please highlight these anchors explicitly in the panel invite and in the shared debrief doc.

Evelyn

Quick read — I like the heatmap. A few bar-raiser notes and concrete interview-level guidance:

Red flags (immediate fail if present):
- No experience shipping at scale (ex: can only point to prototypes or single-node demos)
- Unable to reason about KV cache coherency / cold-start strategies
- No measurable impact on latency/cost in a previous role

Scoring anchors I propose (short):
- 1-2: cannot demonstrate production ownership or system thinking
- 3: solid tactical contributions with gaps in scale/design
- 4: clear owner of production systems, hands-on with performance tradeoffs
- 5: system-level thinking plus strategic tradeoffs and mentoring across teams

Suggested questions to surface tradeoffs (use at least 2):
- Describe a time you reduced tail latency in a production LLM workload — what did you measure and why?
- How do you design an inference cache that supports multi-version models and hot prefix reuse?
- Walk me through a regression you saw post-deploy and your rollback / mitigation decisions.

Debrief template (paste into shared doc):
- Key evidence observed (bullets)
- Risks / unknowns
- Recommendation: Hire/Neutral/No
- Level estimate + one sentence justification

I can take runtime/kernel questions and provide a 10‑minute deep dive if panel wants. Reserve me for those.

-Markus
